Once I worked in a commercial kitchen, I was never able to go back to "home cooking" methods. The tools and methods of the commercial kitchen are not only about creating a safety standard (which they do way better than any home kitchen), but also significantly save on time and cut costs.

In terms of the cutting board question, my system is simple, cheap, and effective:

  • Large color coded plastic NSF certified cutting boards with Microban. You can pick these up for less than $10 on sale from restaurant supply depots. In my home kitchen, they usually last me about a year before the cuts get deep enough to impact use and sanitation.

  • 99 cent spritz bottle from home depot with a diluted bleach with water mixture. (You can't get much cheaper or more effective on cleaning supplies.)

  • After using a board with Raw ingredients that might contain contaminates, simply spray the board AFTER you've cleaned it with soap and water and let the bleach water sit there for a minute before you set it sideways to dry.

Cleaning by itself with soap and water is more than sufficient for non-contaminate foods like carrots or whatnot.

Wood cutting boards are naturally antiseptic, and only require mechanical cleaning.
